question: Article 23-24 of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following fundamental rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right against Exploitation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Articles 23–24 of the Indian Constitution guarantee the Right against Exploitation. (शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार)

• Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour; violation is a punishable offence.

• Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Right to Equality — Articles 14–18 (equality before law, no discrimination, equality of opportunity, abolition of untouchability and titles).

• Right to Freedom — Articles 19–22 (six freedoms, protection in respect of conviction, protection of life and personal liberty, protection against arrest).

• Right to Constitutional Remedies — Article 32, called the “heart and soul of the Constitution” by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

NOTE

• Six Fundamental Rights today: Equality (14–18), Freedom (19–22), Against Exploitation (23–24), Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30), Constitutional Remedies (32).

• The Right to Property (Article 31) was deleted from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 and made a legal right under Article 300A.

question: Who is noted as a pristine Indian Classical Dancer to perform at Salzburg Festival in 2015?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alarmel Valli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alarmel Valli is a celebrated Bharatanatyam exponent of the Pandanallur style who performed at the prestigious Salzburg Festival (Austria) in 2015. (भरतनाट्यम नृत्यांगना)

• She was honoured with the Padma Shri (1991) and the Padma Bhushan (2004), and also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• She founded the dance school Dipasikha Dance Foundation in Chennai and is known for her lyrical, sculpturesque style.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tanjore Balasaraswati (1918–1984) — legendary Bharatanatyam dancer of the Thanjavur hereditary tradition; Padma Vibhushan (1977).

• Kumari Kamala (Kamala Lakshman) — noted Bharatanatyam dancer and film artiste.

• V. Satyanarayana Sarma — well-known Kuchipudi dancer famous for his *stree-vesham* (female roles).

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; Kathak — Uttar Pradesh; Odissi — Odisha; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam — Kerala; Manipuri — Manipur; Sattriya — Assam.

• Bharatanatyam is based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni and was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam.

question: After years of wandering Babur seized Kabul in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1504.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur, after losing Samarkand and years of wandering, captured Kabul in 1504 and made it his base. (काबुल पर अधिकार — 1504)

• Babur succeeded to the throne of Farghana in 1494 at the age of 12 after the death of his father Umar Shaikh Mirza.

• From Kabul he launched raids into India and finally defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat (1526), founding the Mughal Empire.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Babur was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and of Genghis Khan on his mother's side.

• He wrote his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama), in Turki; it was translated into Persian by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan.

• Babur introduced gunpowder artillery and the Tulughma and Araba war tactics in India.

NOTE

• Babur's major battles: Panipat I (1526) vs Ibrahim Lodi; Khanwa (1527) vs Rana Sanga; Chanderi (1528) vs Medini Rai; Ghaghra (1529) vs Afghans.

• He assumed the title Padshah in 1507 and died in 1530 at Agra; he was later buried at Kabul.

question: The Almatti Dam of Karnataka is built over which of the following rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Almatti Dam (Lal Bahadur Shastri Dam) is built on the Krishna river in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, and was completed in 2005. (कृष्णा नदी पर अलमट्टी बांध)

• It is the principal reservoir of the Upper Krishna Irrigation Project and generates hydroelectric power besides irrigating large tracts of north Karnataka.

• The Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar (Western Ghats, Maharashtra) and flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh into the Bay of Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Periyar — the longest river of Kerala; the Mullaperiyar Dam and Idukki Dam are on it.

• Sutlej — a Himalayan river of the Indus system; the Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on it.

• Kaveri — the Krishna Raja Sagar (KRS) and Mettur (Stanley) dams are on the Kaveri.

NOTE

• Tributaries of the Krishna: Bhima, Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Musi, Koyna.

• Other dams on the Krishna: Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam, Prakasam Barrage (Vijayawada).

question: Who among the following won the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Spain won the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022, beating Colombia 1–0 in the final played at the D.Y. Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai on 30 October 2022. (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022)

• The tournament was hosted by India (Bhubaneswar, Goa and Navi Mumbai) — the second FIFA event hosted by India after the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup 2017.

• It was Spain's second U-17 women's title (after 2018); the official mascot was “Ibha”, a snow leopard.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Colombia finished runners-up; Nigeria took third place by beating Germany.

• Japan won this title in 2014, and New Zealand hosted the very first edition in 2008 (won by North Korea).

• India participated as hosts but did not progress beyond the group stage.

NOTE

• FIFA Men's World Cup 2022 was held in Qatar and won by Argentina (beat France on penalties).

• FIFA Women's World Cup 2023 (Australia/New Zealand) was won by Spain, beating England 1–0.

question: Kharchi Pooja of Tripura is a Hindu festival where ______ Hindu Gods are worshiped, including the Earth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kharchi Puja is a famous festival of Tripura in which 14 Hindu deities (Chaturdasha Devata) are worshipped, including Mother Earth. (खारची पूजा — चतुर्दश देवता)

• It is celebrated in the month of Ashadha (June–July) at the Chaturdasha Devata Temple, Old Agartala, and is also called the festival of cleansing of sins.

• The word *kharchi* is derived from *khya* (earth); the ritual is performed by Chantai priests of the Tripuri community, and the festival is celebrated by both tribals and non-tribals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Tripura: Garia Puja, Ker Puja, Ashokastami Mela, Orange and Tourism Festival, Neermahal Water Festival.

• Tripura's capital is Agartala; its major tribal group is the Tripuri (Tipra).

• The Ujjayanta Palace and Neermahal (lake palace) are famous monuments of Tripura.

NOTE

• State festivals often asked in SSC: Bihu — Assam; Hornbill — Nagaland; Wangala — Meghalaya; Losar — Ladakh/Arunachal; Chapchar Kut — Mizoram; Kharchi/Garia — Tripura.

• Tripura became a full-fledged state on 21 January 1972, along with Manipur and Meghalaya.

question: Which among the following dance forms does NOT belong to Chhattisgarh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kajari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kajari (Kajri) is a folk song-and-dance form of Uttar Pradesh (Mirzapur, Varanasi and Banaras region), sung in the rainy month of Sawan; it does not belong to Chhattisgarh. (कजरी — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• Panthi is the dance of the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh, performed on Guru Ghasidas Jayanti.

• Gendi is a stilt dance of the Muria/Gond tribes of Bastar, and Raut Nacha is performed by the Yadav (cowherd) community around Dev Uthni Ekadashi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh: Karma, Saila, Sua (Suwa), Pandwani (folk theatre/ballad), Danda Nacha.

• Pandwani narrates tales of the Mahabharata; its best-known exponent is Teejan Bai (Padma Vibhushan, 2019).

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000; capital Raipur (Naya Raipur/Atal Nagar).

NOTE

• Folk dances of Uttar Pradesh: Kajri, Charkula, Raslila, Nautanki, Jhora, Chhapeli.

• Bastar's famous festival is Bastar Dussehra, said to be the world's longest Dussehra (75 days).

question: The members of ______ are commonly called red algae.
solution_text:
The correct answer is rhodophyceae.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Members of the class Rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the dominance of the red pigment r-phycoerythrin. (लाल शैवाल)

• They are mostly marine, found in warm and deep waters; stored food is floridean starch, and the cell wall contains cellulose, pectin and phycocolloids.

• Examples: Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria, Gelidium — the last two yield agar-agar, used in culture media and ice creams.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Phaeophyceae — brown algae; pigment fucoxanthin; food stored as laminarin/mannitol; e.g. Laminaria, Fucus, Sargassum, Ectocarpus.

• Chlorophyceae — green algae; pigments chlorophyll a and b; food stored as starch; e.g. Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Spirogyra, Ulothrix.

• Poaceae is not an algal class at all — it is the grass family of flowering plants (wheat, rice, bamboo, sugarcane).

NOTE

• Algin is obtained from brown algae and carrageenan from red algae; both are commercially important.

• The largest brown alga is the giant kelp Macrocystis; Chlorella (green alga) is used as a protein-rich food supplement and in space missions.

question: What happened in Bengal, India, in 1770 that resulted in the death of one-third of the population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Famine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Great Bengal Famine of 1770 (Bengali: *Chhiattorer Manvantar*, i.e. the famine of 1176 Bengali era) killed nearly one-third of Bengal's population — an estimated 10 million people. (बंगाल का महा अकाल, 1770)

• It struck during the Dual Government (Dwaidhi Shasan) system introduced by Robert Clive in 1765 after the East India Company obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

• Crop failure was worsened by the Company's rigid land revenue collection and grain hoarding; the disaster led to the Regulating Act of 1773.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Diwani rights were granted by Mughal emperor Shah Alam II by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).

• Warren Hastings ended the dual government in 1772 and made the Company directly responsible for administration.

• The novel Anandamath by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, source of *Vande Mataram*, is set against the backdrop of the famine and the Sannyasi Rebellion.

NOTE

• Other major famines: 1876–78 Great Famine (Madras/Deccan); 1896–97 and 1899–1900 famines; Bengal Famine of 1943 (about 3 million deaths).

• The Famine Commission of 1880 was headed by Sir Richard Strachey.

question: Which of the following is one of the notable works of Vikram Seth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A Suitable Boy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Suitable Boy (1993) is the best-known novel of the Indian writer Vikram Seth; it is one of the longest novels in English ever published in a single volume. (उपन्यासकार विक्रम सेठ)

• Set in post-Independence India of the early 1950s, it follows Mrs Rupa Mehra's search for a suitable husband for her daughter Lata.

• Seth's other works include The Golden Gate, An Equal Music, Two Lives and the travelogue From Heaven Lake (Thomas Cook Travel Book Award). He received the Padma Shri (2007) and the Sahitya Akademi Award (1988).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Show Business — a novel by Shashi Tharoor, who also wrote *The Great Indian Novel* and *An Era of Darkness*.

• Ancient India — a well-known historical work associated with R.C. Majumdar (and a classic school text by R.S. Sharma).

• The Glass Palace — a novel by Amitav Ghosh, author of *The Shadow Lines*, *Sea of Poppies* and *The Hungry Tide*.

NOTE

• *A Suitable Boy* was adapted into a BBC television series (2020) directed by Mira Nair.

• Amitav Ghosh was the first English-language writer to receive the Jnanpith Award (2018).

question: The National Anti-Doping Bill, 2021 targets ______ sector of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sport.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Anti-Doping Bill, 2021 targets the sports sector of India; it seeks to prohibit doping (use of banned performance-enhancing substances) by athletes and support personnel. (राष्ट्रीय डोपिंग रोधी विधेयक)

• It gives statutory status to the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) and the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) and creates a National Board for Anti-Doping in Sports.

• It also sets up an Anti-Doping Appeal Panel and brings Indian law in line with the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport and the WADA Code.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha (27 July 2022) and Rajya Sabha (3 August 2022) and became the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022.

• NADA was established in 2009; WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency) was founded in 1999 with headquarters at Montreal, Canada.

• India is among the countries with a high number of doping violations, which prompted this legislation.

NOTE

• Ministry concerned: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

• National Sports Day is celebrated on 29 August, the birth anniversary of hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand; the highest sporting honour is the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.

question: A Money Bill should be returned to the Lok Sabha within ______ days by Rajya Sabha, either with recommendations or without recommendations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 109 of the Constitution, the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, with or without recommendations. (धन विधेयक — 14 दिन)

• If the Rajya Sabha does not return it within 14 days, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.

• The Lok Sabha may accept or reject the Rajya Sabha's recommendations; thus the Rajya Sabha has only restricted (recommendatory) powers over Money Bills.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A Money Bill is defined in Article 110; it can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the prior recommendation of the President.

• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill, and his decision is final.

• The President can either give assent or withhold assent to a Money Bill but cannot return it for reconsideration.

NOTE

• There is no joint sitting (Article 108) for Money Bills, as disagreement cannot arise.

• Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, but not every Financial Bill is a Money Bill; Financial Bills are covered by Article 117.

question: Who launched Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Jan Urvarak Pariyojana-One Nation One Fertiliser in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Jan Urvarak Pariyojana — One Nation One Fertiliser on 17 October 2022 at the PM Kisan Samman Sammelan, New Delhi (IARI, Pusa). (एक राष्ट्र एक उर्वरक)

• Under the scheme all subsidised fertilisers are sold across the country under a single brand name “Bharat” — Bharat Urea, Bharat DAP, Bharat MOP, Bharat NPK — with a common logo.

• On the same occasion he launched the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samruddhi Kendras (PMKSK) and released the 12th instalment of PM-KISAN.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Narendra Singh Tomar was then the Union Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Minister.

• Mansukh Mandaviya was the Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers, the ministry implementing the scheme.

• Smriti Irani held Women & Child Development, and Amit Shah the Home Ministry.

NOTE

• PM-KISAN (launched 24 February 2019) gives ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments to eligible farmer families.

• Other farmer schemes: PMFBY (2016) crop insurance, Soil Health Card (2015), e-NAM (2016), PM-KUSUM (2019).

question: In which of the following articles, "Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights" is mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 13.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 13 is titled “Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights” and declares that any law which contravenes a Fundamental Right shall be void to the extent of the contravention. (मौलिक अधिकारों से असंगत विधियाँ)

• It is the basis of the power of judicial review, exercised by the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226).

• Article 13 gives a wide meaning to “law” — ordinances, orders, bye-laws, rules, regulations, notifications, customs and usages.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 12 defines the term “State” for the purposes of Part III.

• Article 14 provides equality before law and equal protection of the laws.

• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

NOTE

• Article 13(4), added by the 24th Amendment (1971), says a constitutional amendment under Article 368 is not “law” under Article 13 — but the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) established the Basic Structure doctrine.

• Related doctrines: Doctrine of Eclipse, Doctrine of Severability and Doctrine of Waiver flow from Article 13.

question: Money multiplier uses which of the following monetary instruments for its calculation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cash reserve ratio.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The money multiplier is calculated as 1 / CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) — it shows the maximum amount of money the banking system can create from a given quantity of high-powered money. (मुद्रा गुणक = 1/नकद आरक्षित अनुपात)

• CRR is the percentage of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that must be kept as cash with the RBI; no interest is paid on it.

• A lower CRR means a higher money multiplier and greater credit creation; a higher CRR contracts money supply.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Repo rate — rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities.

• Reverse repo rate — rate at which the RBI borrows from commercial banks, absorbing liquidity.

• Bank rate — long-term lending rate of the RBI without collateral; linked to the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF).

NOTE

• SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) is the share of NDTL kept in cash, gold or approved securities with the bank itself.

• Quantitative tools of the RBI: CRR, SLR, Repo, Reverse Repo, Bank Rate, OMO; qualitative tools: margin requirements, moral suasion, credit rationing.

question: लड़कों में बढ़ता हुआ 'स्वरयंत्र' गले के सामने की ओर सुस्पष्ट उभरे भाग के रूप में दिखाई देता है, जिसे ______ कहते हैं।
solution_text:
The correct answer is कंठमणि (Adam's apple).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During puberty in boys the larynx (voice box / स्वरयंत्र) grows larger and its thyroid cartilage projects out in front of the throat as a visible bulge called the Adam's apple (कंठमणि).

• This enlargement of the larynx makes the vocal cords longer and thicker, which is why boys' voices become deeper (hoarse) during adolescence.

• It is a secondary sexual character caused by the male hormone testosterone, secreted by the testes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Adrenalin (एड्रिनेलिन) — the “fight or flight” hormone secreted by the adrenal medulla; also called epinephrine.

• Corn (कॉर्न) — a thickened, hardened patch of skin, usually on the foot; not related to the larynx.

• Gullet (ग्रसिका) — another name for the oesophagus, the food pipe carrying food from the pharynx to the stomach.

NOTE

• Secondary sexual characters in girls at puberty are controlled by oestrogen, secreted by the ovaries.

• The pituitary gland is called the master gland; it secretes growth hormone, FSH and LH which regulate puberty.

question: गंगूबाई हंगल, हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत की ख्याल (Khayal) शैली की ______ राज्य की एक भारतीय गायिका थीं, जो अपनी गहरी और दमदार आवाज के लिए जानी जाती थीं।
solution_text:
The correct answer is कर्नाटक (Karnataka).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gangubai Hangal (1913–2009) was an Indian singer of the Khayal style of Hindustani classical music, born at Dharwad in Karnataka. (किराना घराना की गायिका)

• She belonged to the Kirana Gharana and was a disciple of Sawai Gandharva (Rambhau Kundgolkar); she was famous for her deep, powerful, masculine-sounding voice.

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1971) and the Padma Vibhushan (2002), besides the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1973).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other great musicians from Karnataka: Bhimsen Joshi (Kirana Gharana, Bharat Ratna 2008), Mallikarjun Mansur, Basavaraj Rajguru.

• Khayal is the dominant vocal genre of Hindustani music; Dhrupad is the older, more austere form.

• Main Hindustani gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Kirana, Agra, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Rampur-Sahaswan.

NOTE

• Carnatic music's Trinity: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

• Amir Khusrau is credited with developing Khayal, Qawwali, Tarana and instruments like the sitar and tabla.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of "agro based industries"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron and steel industry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The iron and steel industry is a mineral-based (metallurgical) industry, since its raw materials are iron ore, coking coal, limestone, dolomite and manganese — not agricultural produce. (खनिज आधारित उद्योग)

• Agro-based industries use agricultural products as raw material — e.g. cotton textile, jute, silk, woollen textile, sugar, vegetable oil, leather, tea, coffee and food processing.

• India's iron and steel plants include Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur, Burnpur and the country's first modern plant, TISCO at Jamshedpur (1907).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Leather industry uses hides and skins obtained from animals — hence agro/animal based.

• Vegetable oil industry uses oilseeds such as groundnut, mustard, soyabean and sunflower.

• Cotton textile industry is India's largest agro-based industry; the first modern mill was set up in Mumbai in 1854.

NOTE

• Classification of industries by raw material: agro-based, mineral-based, marine-based, forest-based.

• India is the second largest producer of crude steel in the world after China; the National Steel Policy was revised in 2017.

question: According to census 2011, the only Indian state having negative decadal population growth rate between 2001- 11 is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, Nagaland was the only Indian state with a negative decadal population growth rate (–0.58%) during 2001–2011. (ऋणात्मक दशकीय वृद्धि दर)

• The all-India decadal growth rate for 2001–2011 was 17.7%, the lowest growth in any decade since Independence.

• The highest decadal growth among states was recorded by Meghalaya (27.9%); among UTs, Dadra & Nagar Haveli (55.9%).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th after Independence; its motto was “Our Census, Our Future”.

• India's population in 2011 was 121.08 crore; sex ratio 943; literacy rate 74.04%; density 382 persons per sq km.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest density — Bihar (1106); lowest — Arunachal Pradesh (17).

NOTE

• Highest literacy — Kerala (94%); lowest — Bihar (61.8%). Highest sex ratio — Kerala (1084); lowest — Haryana (879).

• The first census in India was held in 1872 under Lord Mayo and the first complete/synchronous census in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: Who was the founder of the Widow Remarriage Association (1861)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahadev Govind Ranade.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahadev Govind Ranade founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1861 at Bombay to promote the remarriage of Hindu widows. (विधवा पुनर्विवाह संघ, 1861)

• He was a judge of the Bombay High Court, a founder of the Prarthana Samaj, the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) and the Deccan Education Society, and a founding figure of the Indian National Congress.

• He also started the Indian National Social Conference (1887) and is called the father of Indian economics.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in 1867 at Bombay.

• R.G. Bhandarkar was an eminent orientalist and social reformer associated with the Prarthana Samaj; the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune, is named after him.

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj (1828) and campaigned against Sati, abolished by Lord William Bentinck in 1829.

NOTE

• The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 was passed largely due to the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar under Governor-General Lord Dalhousie/Canning.

• Vishnu Shastri Pandit founded the Widow Remarriage Association work in Maharashtra along with Ranade; D.K. Karve founded the Widow Home at Poona (1899).

question: The strong gravitational pull exerted by the ______ on the earth's surface causes the tides.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sun and moon only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tides are caused by the gravitational pull of the Sun and the Moon on the earth's water surface, along with the centrifugal force produced by the earth's rotation. (ज्वार-भाटा)

• The Moon's tide-generating force is about 2.2 times that of the Sun, because although the Sun is far more massive it is much farther away.

• Spring tides (highest) occur on full moon and new moon when the Sun, Earth and Moon are in a straight line (syzygy); Neap tides (lowest) occur in the first and third quarters when they are at right angles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• High tide and low tide occur roughly twice a day, about 12 hours 25 minutes apart.

• Tides help in navigation into ports, fishing, desilting of harbours and in generating tidal energy.

• India's proposed tidal power sites are the Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat (Gujarat) and the Sundarbans (West Bengal).

NOTE

• The Bay of Fundy (Canada) records the world's highest tidal range (about 15–16 m).

• Tides are different from ocean currents (caused by winds, temperature and salinity differences) and waves (caused by winds).

question: The thickness of a wrestling mat should be between ______ centimetres.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 and 7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the standards followed for wrestling (कुश्ती), the thickness of the wrestling mat should be between 5 and 7 centimetres, so that it absorbs the impact of throws and falls.

• A modern competition mat is a 12 m × 12 m square containing a circular contest area of 9 m diameter, with a red passivity zone of 1 m along its inner edge.

• The international governing body of wrestling is United World Wrestling (UWW), formerly FILA, with headquarters at Corsier-sur-Vevey, Switzerland.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Olympic wrestling has two styles — Freestyle and Greco-Roman; in Greco-Roman, holds below the waist are not allowed.

• A wrestling bout consists of two periods of 3 minutes each with a 30-second break.

• Famous Indian wrestlers: Khashaba Jadhav (first individual Olympic medal for India, 1952), Sushil Kumar, Yogeshwar Dutt, Sakshi Malik, Bajrang Punia, Ravi Dahiya.

NOTE

• Terms of wrestling: Half Nelson, Takedown, Pin (Fall), Bridge, Escape, Passivity, Technical Superiority.

• India's traditional wrestling arena is called an akhara; the Rustam-e-Hind title is associated with the great Gama Pahalwan.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Inflammable substances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glass.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Inflammable (flammable) substances are those which have a very low ignition temperature and catch fire easily — such as petrol, alcohol, LPG and kerosene. (ज्वलनशील पदार्थ)

• Glass is a non-combustible material made mainly of silica (SiO₂); it does not catch fire and hence is not inflammable.

• The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its ignition temperature; a substance cannot burn below it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) is mainly butane with propane; ethyl mercaptan is added to give it a smell so that leaks are detected.

• Three conditions necessary for combustion: fuel, air (oxygen) and attainment of ignition temperature.

• Water is not used to extinguish oil and electrical fires; CO₂ is the best extinguisher for them.

NOTE

• Types of combustion: rapid (LPG burning), spontaneous (phosphorus), explosion (crackers).

• Zones of a candle flame: innermost dark zone (unburnt vapours), middle luminous yellow zone (partial combustion), outermost blue zone (complete combustion, hottest).

question: Which monument of Khilji dynasty in Delhi has the utilization of red sandstone?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alai Darwaza.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Alai Darwaza, built by Alauddin Khilji in 1311, is the southern gateway of the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in the Qutub Minar complex, Delhi; it is made of red sandstone inlaid with white marble. (अलाई दरवाजा)

• It is regarded as the first true dome and true arch built in India on scientific lines, marking the beginning of the Turkish/Imperial style of Indo-Islamic architecture.

• Alauddin also began the Alai Minar, intended to be twice the height of the Qutub Minar, but it was left unfinished after his death.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Moti Masjid — built by Aurangzeb in the Red Fort, Delhi (and another by Shah Jahan in the Agra Fort), made of white marble.

• Victoria Memorial — built at Kolkata (1906–1921) in memory of Queen Victoria, made of white Makrana marble.

• Charminar — built at Hyderabad in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty.

NOTE

• The Qutub Minar complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993); the Minar was begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

• Khilji dynasty (1290–1320) rulers: Jalaluddin Khilji → Alauddin Khilji → Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah; Alauddin introduced market (price) control and the Dagh and Chehra system.

question: Who among the following succeeded the throne of the Mauryan Empire after the death of Chandragupta Maurya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bindusara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bindusara (c. 297–273 BCE), the son of Chandragupta Maurya, succeeded him to the throne of the Mauryan Empire. (मौर्य सम्राट बिंदुसार)

• He was known as Amitraghata (“slayer of foes”) to the Greeks as Amitrochates, and the Jain texts call him Simhasena.

• He followed the Ajivika sect; the Greek ambassador Deimachus (sent by Antiochus I) and Dionysius (sent by Ptolemy II) visited his court.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ashoka, son of Bindusara, ruled from about 268 to 232 BCE and fought the Kalinga War (261 BCE).

• Dasharatha was a grandson of Ashoka who ruled after him and granted the Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas.

• Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) belonged to the Gupta dynasty, not the Mauryas; the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited during his reign.

NOTE

• Mauryan succession: Chandragupta Maurya → Bindusara → Ashoka → Dasharatha → ... → Brihadratha (killed by Pushyamitra Shunga, 185 BCE).

• Ashoka's edicts were deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837; the Sarnath Lion Capital is India's National Emblem.
